why: The other noise class worth pinning. A percentage deviation computed over a few dozen rows carries almost no information — five extra rows on a 38-row table is a 13% swing — and treating it as signal is how a monitor earns its way onto the permanent ignore list. The reasoning is arithmetic, not domain knowledge, so it holds for any small table anywhere.

monitor_rows.message: Row count is 13.2% above the trailing 7-day average of 38 rows. Absolute change: +5 rows. This table has never exceeded 60 rows and grows by a handful of rows most weeks.
